name: Critical minerals
value: US gallium ban pause ends 27 Nov; licences stay
summary: China's one-year pause of its gallium, germanium and antimony ban on the US reaches its 27 Nov end date; licensing stays
state: China's one-year suspension of its ban on gallium, germanium and antimony exports to the US runs to 27 Nov, after which the ban could return, while its wider export-licensing regime stays in place (SCMP). On 9 Nov China extended a separate suspension of controls on five rare earths and related technology to 10 Jan 2027, but April 2025 controls on seven rare earths remain in force (S&P Global). Searches on 27 Nov found no announcement on the gallium pause and no production stoppages outside China linked to export bans, so Watch holds.
for_you: Makers of chips, defence electronics, magnets and batteries outside China are most exposed; past curbs have led to input shortages and delays some months after they took effect.
rubric_hit: Watch: Chinese export licensing in force and a US export-ban pause expiring 27 Nov; no reported stoppages outside China

why: Rare earths, gallium, germanium and graphite are chokepoints for chips, EVs and defence — and China dominates processing.
drivers: Export controls, trade disputes, mine outages, stockpiling.

rubric.alert: Export bans in force that are causing reported production stoppages outside China.
rubric.watch: New export controls announced or licensing slowed.
rubric.normal: No new export restrictions in the past month.
